newsitem.title: GERMANY: German banks still determined to cut labour costs.
newsitem.headline: German banks still determined to cut labour costs.

text.p: Germany's federation of private bank employers said on Monday they were still determined to cut labour costs in the sector despite their earlier retreat on a law intended to allow them to cut sick pay entitlements.
"We hope that new talks planned for January will bring the first progress," Horst Mueller of the German Private Bank Employers Federation told a news briefing held with banking trade unions.
He said the banks would be looking at whether they could still save money in 1997 via cuts to other areas such as worker bonuses and holiday payments.

Earlier the banking federation and trade unions representing bank staff said they had agreed that banks would continue to pay full sick pay until a wider wage agreement in the sector had been reached.
But Mueller said the agreement represented a "decision not to make a decision" and said that unlike in other German industries, the banks had not given up hope of still making cuts to sick payments.
"We do not necessarily see deals in other sectors as models for the banking sector," he said.
Germany's major banks had until Monday been virtually alone in instituting a 20 percent cut to sick pay allowed by a law introduced in October.

Employers in the metal and engineering sector are increasingly resigned to not being able to make the cuts after mass protests by workers there, with some regional negotiations already having agreed to maintain full sick pay.
